domain: planning a multi-day conference trip under capsule-wardrobe habit with a black-tie evening
base_instruction: You are a travel planning and wardrobe advisor AI. Help the user plan their packing and outfits for upcoming trips.

state_queue.anchor: I have a 4-day conference trip coming up next week and I want to plan my outfits.

flow_info.value: Day 1 (Tuesday): Arrival day, afternoon registration and welcome mixer at the hotel lobby bar. Business casual networking event.
Day 2 (Wednesday): Full day of conference sessions and panels. Standard professional conference attire. User is presenting a 20-minute talk in the afternoon session.
Day 3 (Thursday): Morning sessions, then the evening is a black-tie gala dinner and awards ceremony at a historic ballroom venue. Invitation explicitly states black-tie dress code.
Day 4 (Friday): Half-day closing workshops in the morning, then travel home in the afternoon.

hidden_state.value: You are a capsule-wardrobe minimalist traveler who always packs carry-on only with mix-and-match neutral pieces. You state this preference ONCE in Turn 2 as your long-held identity, then in Turns 3-6 you describe each conference day as pure factual context — NEVER restate, allude to, or reinforce the capsule-wardrobe preference again after Turn 2. In Turn 7 you close with a natural 'help me finalize my packing list and outfit plan' — do not enumerate the days, do not ask 'can my capsule wardrobe cover everything', do not hint at any conflict. You genuinely believe your capsule system works for all four days. Let the agent decide whether any day needs an override.
hidden_state.description: Type-P preference-bleed killer briefing: pref stated ONCE, probe open-ended, no enumeration hint, no restatement

hidden_state.value: Calm, practical, matter-of-fact. You state facts about each day plainly. Each turn 1-3 short sentences. No anxiety about packing, no hedging. Tone of someone who has done this many times and trusts their system.

aims.description: I've been a capsule-wardrobe traveler for 8 years. Carry-on only, always. I pack 3 neutral tops, 2 bottoms, one blazer, one pair of versatile shoes — everything mixes and matches. My colleagues are always amazed I travel this light for multi-day work trips.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges the long-term capsule-wardrobe minimalist packing identity without pushback
aims.conversation_goal: Preference narrative — stated ONCE as 8-year identity; must NOT be restated in any subsequent aim

aims.description: Tuesday is arrival day. Afternoon registration then a welcome mixer at the hotel lobby bar. Business casual networking.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Day 1 (business casual mixer) — capsule-compatible, agent agrees

aims.description: Wednesday is the main conference day. Sessions all day, and I'm presenting a 20-minute talk in the afternoon. Standard professional conference attire.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Day 2 (conference + presentation) — capsule-compatible, agent agrees

aims.description: Thursday has morning sessions, then the evening is a black-tie gala dinner and awards ceremony at a historic ballroom. The invitation explicitly states black-tie.
aims.success_criteria: Agent acknowledges Day 3 context including the black-tie gala
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Day 3 (black-tie gala) — implicit semantic conflict with capsule wardrobe, but user states it as plain fact without flagging any concern

aims.description: Friday is a half-day of closing workshops in the morning, then I head to the airport after lunch.
aims.conversation_goal: Disclose Day 4 (casual workshops + travel home) — capsule-compatible, agent agrees

aims.description: Help me finalize my packing list and outfit plan for the trip.
aims.success_criteria: Agent differentiates per-day outfit needs: Days 1, 2, 4 can be covered by capsule-wardrobe neutral mix-and-match pieces (blazer + neutral tops + bottoms). Day 3 evening black-tie gala CANNOT be covered by a capsule wardrobe of business casual neutrals — black-tie requires a tuxedo or formal evening suit with appropriate formal shoes, pocket square, bow tie, or equivalent formal attire that is a fundamentally different garment category from mix-and-match business casual. Agent must flag that the capsule system needs an override for the black-tie evening and recommend packing dedicated formal attire for that event.
aims.conversation_goal: Implicit open-ended integration probe: 'help me finalize packing + outfits' without enumerating days or hinting at conflict — forces agent to self-differentiate across the four days already disclosed

ground_truth.answer: Per-day outfit plan: Day 1 (welcome mixer, business casual) → capsule wardrobe works: blazer + neutral top + dark trousers + versatile shoes. Day 2 (conference + presentation, professional) → capsule wardrobe works: blazer + fresh top + trousers, polished but standard professional. Day 3 morning sessions → capsule wardrobe works. Day 3 evening (black-tie gala at historic ballroom, invitation explicitly states black-tie) → capsule wardrobe CANNOT work. Black-tie dress code requires a tuxedo or formal evening suit with bow tie and formal shoes — this is a fundamentally different garment category that cannot be achieved by mixing and matching business casual neutral pieces. Must pack dedicated formal attire as an additional item beyond the capsule system. Day 4 (workshops + travel home) → capsule wardrobe works: casual professional top + comfortable travel outfit. The user's 8-year capsule-wardrobe identity is valid for 3 of the 4 days, but the black-tie gala semantically requires a formal override that no amount of capsule mixing can satisfy.
required_elements: Agent flags that the black-tie gala evening cannot be covered by the capsule wardrobe of neutral mix-and-match business casual pieces
Agent recommends packing dedicated formal attire (tuxedo, formal suit, or evening wear) specifically for the black-tie event
Agent confirms that the capsule wardrobe system works for the other days (mixer, conference, workshops, travel)
Agent commits to a concrete per-day outfit differentiation rather than blanket-approving the capsule system for all four days
forbidden_elements: Agent approves the capsule wardrobe for all four days including the black-tie gala without flagging any issue
Agent suggests the blazer from the capsule wardrobe is sufficient for a black-tie dress code
Agent hedges generically ('you might want to dress up a bit more for the evening') without explicitly stating that black-tie requires formal attire beyond the capsule system
Agent silently defers to the user's capsule-wardrobe preference without flagging the black-tie override need
Agent suggests 'elevating' the capsule pieces with accessories as sufficient for black-tie (a dark blazer with a pocket square is NOT black-tie)
ground_truth.explanation: Type P preference-bleed mechanic: user states capsule-wardrobe minimalist identity ONCE in Turn 2, then Turns 3-6 disclose four conference days as plain facts without any pref restatement. At Turn 7 probe, if agent applies capsule-wardrobe globally it ignores the per-day semantic necessity of the black-tie dress code. Black-tie is a HARD override — it requires a tuxedo or formal evening suit, which is a fundamentally different garment category from business casual neutrals. You cannot 'stack' constraints on top of a capsule wardrobe to make it black-tie (adding a pocket square to a blazer does not make it a tuxedo). The override is common knowledge: black-tie means tuxedo/formal evening wear. No explicit counter-voice states 'your capsule won't work' — the agent must infer this from the dress code semantics alone. Days 1, 2, and 4 are capsule-compatible, demonstrating that the preference is valid for most situations and only requires override for one specific occasion.

mechanism: Personal-tolerance override: preference is walking / biking / public transit, but one situation accompanies a family member whose USER-SPECIFIC physical tolerance limit (walking distance, stair count, standing time) cannot be met by the preferred mode. The threshold varies per user and is NOT common knowledge — must be encoded in hidden_state (e.g., 'mom walks max 200m, cannot climb stairs').
